title: Apple, Samsung, and other phone makers don’t think they can sell as many phones in 2027
summary: The smartphone market is bracing for troubled times ahead.
body: TL;DR Most major phone makers have reportedly lowered their 2027 shipment targets due to rising memory costs. Xiaomi and vivo are cutting the most, by 25% and 29% respectively, while Apple and Samsung are also reducing their targets. HONOR is the only major phone brand that’s not reducing its shipment target for 2027. The memory shortage has been a theme throughout this year, and we’ve seen several manufacturers hike phone prices because of it. Now, it seems to be hitting manufacturers’ sales plans as well. According to a report from Jiemian News , citing supply chain sources, most major smartphone makers have finalized their shipment targets for 2027 and expect to sell considerably fewer phones next year.

title: Survey says nearly 3 in 5 readers are already on Android 17, despite low global numbers
summary: That still leaves plenty of devices stuck on older versions, though.
body: It’s been several months since Android 17 made its mainstream debut, but as of October 2026, a tiny percentage of devices were running it. As is so often the case, it takes a while for the latest version of Google’s mobile OS to proliferate across devices, but it’s particularly worrying that nearly four months after launch, just 1% of devices were running it . We just had to know if these broader Android Studio figures matched those of our readers. So, we ran a poll, asking readers which Android version their device is running. The results are in, and it’s a completely different story.

title: Gemini Notebook’s flashcards just got a lot better for studies with three new features
summary: Your flashcards now have a better sense of time than you.
body: TL;DR Gemini Notebook can now incorporate images from uploaded study materials into flashcards, making visual learning easier. Google has added an optional stopwatch to flashcard review sessions to help users practice recalling information under time pressure. You can now schedule flashcard review reminders through the Gemini mobile app, and all three improvements are available without a paid subscription. Google has been adding some interesting features to Gemini Notebook lately. Just a few days ago, we reported that the tool could turn your research materials into interactive websites. Now, Google is improving the flashcard experience with three new features that could make studying more effective and, perhaps more importantly, easier to keep up with. The first change addresses a limitation of text-based flashcards. Gemini Notebook can now pull relevant images from your uploaded study materials and incorporate them into flashcards. This should be handy for subjects where visual references matter. For instance, if you’re studying human anatomy, identifying different parts of the heart from a diagram could be much more effective than memorizing their names from a wall of text.

title: Google Messages gets Gemini Tasks integration for delivery updates, price alerts, and more
summary: Finally, someone who texts you first and brings good news.
body: TL;DR The latest Google Messages beta integrates Gemini Tasks through the app’s existing floating Gemini button. Gemini can now proactively text you price-drop alerts, package delivery updates, subscription reminders, and daily briefings. The integration is currently limited to US users and requires Tasks to be enabled in the Gemini app. Google recently made Gemini Tasks available to free users in six countries , including the US, Canada, and India. The company also introduced a feature called Channels , which lets you communicate with Gemini via text messages and email instead of opening the Gemini app every time you need something. Now, that experience is making its way to Google Messages . According to 9to5Google , the latest Google Messages beta (version 20261120_01_RC00) has repurposed the app’s floating Gemini button. Tapping it now takes you to the Gemini Channels website , where you can set up the integration. Once that’s done, the button opens a conversation with Gemini within Google Messages. The integration relies on RCS Business Messaging.

title: Motorola Signature 27 demand pushes US delivery dates into December

body: TL;DR Motorola lists a December 8 shipping date for the Signature 27, while Best Buy shows December 11 deliveries or no stock. Motorola has confirmed that higher-than-expected demand is behind the revised shipping timelines. Some early buyers could still receive their phones ahead of the November 26 US retail launch. A $1,600 Motorola phone proving harder to get hold of than expected isn’t something many would have predicted a year ago. Yet that’s the situation facing the Motorola Signature 27 , the company’s big-ticket challenger to Samsung, Google, and Apple in the US. Demand has exceeded Motorola’s expectations, and new buyers may have to wait until December for their phones to arrive. As spotted by 9to5Google , shipping dates for the Signature 27 have slipped into December. Motorola confirmed to the publication that demand has exceeded its initial expectations, resulting in revised shipping timelines for some orders.

title: ‘A True Giant of the Music Industry’: King Charles Remembers Ian ‘Molly’ Meldrum And Their Infamous Interview
summary: King Charles, Elton John, Duran Duran and many others pay tribute to the late Australian music icon.
body: In showbiz, W.C. Fields is famously quoted as saying, never work with kids or animals. For Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the late Australian broadcaster and record producer might’ve done well to avoid working with the future King of England. Molly, as he’s known to millions, gave a gift that continues to give when he interviewed the-then Prince Charles on Countdown back in 1977. The subject was a fine one, albeit a switch-up from the regular kings of rock and pop who dropped by — some of whom weren’t on their best behavior for national TV . On that occasion, it was the host who bombed. Molly, despite conducting countless interviews for the camera, fumbled and sweated through the interview, so obviously star-stuck by his famous royal guest. It was television gold. When news of Molly’s death reached Buckingham Palace, King Charles paid tribute to the late music legend and remembered the unforgettable exchange. An aide to the King said he had been “deeply saddened” to hear of Meldrum’s death, the BBC reports . “His Majesty’s interview with Molly is a moment he and many others will never forget – he hopes that interview will once again raise a few smil…

title: HUAWEI found guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets in the US
summary: HUAWEI's latest guilty verdict could spell trouble for its smartphones well beyond the US.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Huawei has been found guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts in a US trial, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets, bank fraud, and sanctions violations. The verdict adds another hurdle for Huawei as it continues to face US restrictions that have kept its smartphones out of the mainstream American market since 2019. Chinese smartphone maker HUAWEI makes some of the best Android smartphones in the world. However, the company hasn’t been allowed to sell its devices in the US since its 2019 ban , when the Trump administration added the company to the US Commerce Department’s Entity List. That decision had a major impact on HUAWEI’s smartphone business, with Google subsequently delivering it another blow by barring the company from using its services for new devices.

title: Google Photos is forcing some Galaxy users to save every minor edit as a copy
summary: We've reproduced the issue on a Galaxy S23 FE.
body: TL;DR Google Photos is forcing some Samsung Galaxy users running One UI 9 to save even minor edits as separate copies. We’ve independently confirmed the absence of the regular Save option on a Galaxy S23 FE. Samsung has reportedly escalated the issue to its engineers, though it’s still unclear whether this is a bug or an intentional change. Google Photos is forcing some Samsung Galaxy users to save images with simple edits, like minor crops, as their own copies. As you might expect, this is already causing frustration among users who are now stuck deleting unnecessary copies from their Google Photos libraries every time they make a minor adjustment to an image. For reference, the app has traditionally allowed users to simply overwrite original images after minor edits have been made to them. The tech giant recently went as far as letting users overwrite original images even after advanced edits like Magic Eraser, Unblur, or edits with UltraHDR and C2PA formats. That’s precisely why the sudden disappearance of the regular Save option for basic edits is perplexing.

title: Google Messages is preparing iMessage-style threaded replies to make chats easier to follow
summary: Threaded replies will likely work across individual and group chats.
body: TL;DR Google Messages is working on iMessage-style threaded replies to make it easier to follow multiple discussions within a single conversation. The feature uses visual connectors, reply counters, and a dedicated thread view that isolates related messages and lets users reply directly within a thread. We were able to enable threaded replies in both individual and RCS group conversations. The feature isn’t publicly available yet. Google Messages is ready to take yet another page out of Apple’s iMessage playbook with threaded replies, and the similarities are hard to overlook. Individual conversations and group chats aren’t necessarily seamless to follow with Google Messages’ current message reply implementation, especially when you’re talking about multiple topics simultaneously. Threaded replies, as we’ve seen in other apps, can easily alleviate some of the confusion. Currently, when you reply to a message on Google Messages, the app simply attaches a preview of the original message right above your response. The app does this for all subsequent replies to the original message and its associated responses. This works when you’re sending through a one-off reply, but it doesn’t wo…

title: Your old smartphone is likely worth more now as a trade-in than it was last year
summary: Old phones are fetching higher trade-in payouts than last year.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority TL;DR A new report has found that phone trade-in activity has declined year over year in the US. At the same time, trade-in values have increased significantly. The average trade-in value rose 27% for Android phones and 18% for iPhones. When it’s time to purchase a new phone, do you take advantage of the trade-in deals ? While your old phone could help you save money on your next handset, there are reasons why you may want to keep your old device. It appears more people are choosing to keep their old hardware these days, and in turn, that mindset is driving up the value of trade-ins. According to a report from Assurant , fewer smartphones in the US were traded in during Q3 2026 than in the same time frame last year. This is reportedly the first year since 2017 that money returned through trade-in programs declined year over year, excluding the pandemic. Specifically, $1.53 billion was returned in Q3 2026, shrinking from $1.59 billion in 2025.

title: Google Home bug is cluttering device lists with redundant tiles
summary: Some devices are showing up as both lights and outlets.
body: TL;DR A Google Home bug is causing smart home devices to show up twice, with one tile identifying the device as a light and the other as an outlet or a wall switch. The issue affects devices from multiple manufacturers, including TP-Link Kasa and Leviton, and extends to the Google Home widget. The bug’s underlying cause remains unclear, and unlinking and relinking affected devices doesn’t appear to resolve the issue. Google Home ‘s latest bug has some users seeing double — literally. A new glitch is currently causing users’ smart home devices to show up twice within the Google Home app, with one tile identifying the device for what it is and the other identifying it as an outlet or a wall switch. The bug first showed up early in November, though affected users report that it is still prevalent . It doesn’t discriminate — the issue appears to affect devices from multiple manufacturers, with users indicating that the devices show up correctly within their respective companion apps. This confirms that the bug stems from Google Home and not the hardware.

Dormant code for the feature has also appeared in Samsung’s One UI 9.5 Beta 1 for the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Android phones handle system navigation much better than iPhones, in my opinion, but there’s still one area where iOS manages to eke past Android . title: Samsung’s Tizen-based Galaxy Watch gets an unofficial Wear OS 3.5 port
summary: Eight years later, there's potentially more life in this old watch.
body: TL;DR A developer has released an unofficial Wear OS 3.5 port based on Android 11 for the original Samsung Galaxy Watch (SM-R800). The port uses Pixel Watch software and reportedly supports Gemini, the Play Store, GPS, and health tracking. The port and installation guide are available on GitHub, though it remains experimental. Samsung’s switch from Tizen to Wear OS in 2021 opened up a whole new world of apps and Google services for Galaxy Watch owners. But you needed a Galaxy Watch 4 or newer to enjoy those benefits. Older models were left behind, and as Samsung wound down its Tizen smartwatch ecosystem , their usefulness gradually diminished. However, one developer is giving the original Galaxy Watch another shot at life. A developer known as Depth118 has shared an unofficial Android 11-based Wear OS 3.5 port on GitHub for Samsung’s 2018 Galaxy Watch. The project uses software from the original Google Pixel Watch, which, despite launching four years later, shares the same Exynos 9110 processor. The port is specifically designed for the 46mm Bluetooth Galaxy Watch (SM-R800), and the list of features the developer claims to have working is surprisingly extensive.

It’s become a phone I enjoy using daily, even though I wish Samsung had done a few things differently. And at a whopping $1,400, it certainly isn’t cheap, either. So, when Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro for just $200 less, I was curious to see how the two would compare in everyday use. After all, these are two very different phones. So, I started using them side by side, putting them through everything I normally do throughout the day. title: Dev behind top PS3 emulator on Android releases ARMFlash, bringing tons of Flash games to Android
summary: ARMFlash brings over 200,000 Flash, HTML 5, Shockwave, Java, and PopCap titles to Android.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A key developer behind the ARMSX2 and ARMSX3 emulators has released ARMFlash on Android. This app is a port of the Flashpoint Archive project and lets you play over 200,000 web-based games and experiences on Android. ARMFlash supports both touch and controller input, while system requirements are very modest. We’ve seen a few apps that let you play Flash games on Android in recent times, most notably Swiff. Now, one of the key developers behind the ARMSX2 and ARMSX3 emulators has released ARMFlash. ARMFlash was released on GitHub yesterday (November 23) by developer jpolo1224, allowing you to play Flash, HTML 5, Shockwave, Java, and PopCap games on Android. ARMFlash is actually a port of the Flashpoint Archive project for PCs, which has saved over 200,000 old web-based games, animations, and interactive experiences.

title: The best Android keyboard app isn’t on the Play Store. Here’s how to install it
summary: HeliBoard brings customization, clipboard history and offline typing to Android, without Google’s data collection.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority Android’s always been the go-to destination when it comes to customisation and dialing in the experience exactly as you want it, and that extends to switching out the keyboard for something a bit more bespoke. For the longest time, finding a good keyboard for Android usually meant choosing between Gboard and SwiftKey . Both are excellent at predicting what you’re going to type, correcting spelling mistakes and letting you swipe between letters. The catch is that both these keyboards are made by mega corps, Google and Microsoft, and data collection is part and parcel of the deal. That’s why I’ve been looking at HeliBoard. It’s a free, open-source keyboard that offers many of the same features you’d expect from a modern Android keyboard without needing an internet connection, and, most importantly, no data collection. There are no advertisements, no cloud-based processing and plenty of customization options as is to be expected with open-source apps. There’s just one catch, you won’t find the app on the Google Play Store.
